detect.visual_cues: Blue Alipay app chrome. Screens with a bank-card form (card number, expiry, CVV), a red or grey failure banner, a passport-upload prompt, a QR payment code page, or a mini-program named TourCard.

entries.title: Set up Alipay before you fly
entries.why: Most shops, taxis and metro gates in China take mobile payment only. Setting up at home on Wi-Fi takes 10 minutes and avoids doing it jet-lagged with no data.
steps: Install Alipay from the App Store or Google Play. Outside China it opens in English automatically.
Sign up with your own mobile number (any country) and enter the SMS code. No Chinese number or Chinese bank account is needed.
Tap Me > Bank Cards > Add Now. Set a 6-digit payment password, then add one mainstream credit card: Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Discover, Diners Club or UnionPay.
Tap Me > Settings > Account & Security > Identity Verification. Upload your passport photo page and do the face check. Do this now, not later.
entries.fallback: If the card will not link, see Card won't link. If you prefer not to link a card, open TourCard inside Alipay as a prepaid wallet.

entries.title: Card won't link to Alipay
entries.why: Alipay asks your bank to approve the card. Banks often block an unfamiliar Chinese merchant, and debit, prepaid and virtual cards fail more than mainstream credit cards.
steps: Try a different card first: a credit card from a major bank on another network (Visa if Mastercard failed, or the reverse). This fixes most cases.
Check that the name on the card, on your passport and in your Alipay profile match exactly.
Finish Identity Verification (Me > Settings > Account & Security > Identity Verification), then add the card again. Some link failures are really verification failures.
Call your bank: ask them to allow international online transactions and confirm the card supports online verification (3-D Secure). Then retry once.
entries.fallback: Open TourCard inside Alipay and top it up from your card instead. If that also fails, withdraw cash at a Bank of China ATM with your foreign card.

entries.title: No SMS code from Alipay
entries.why: The code goes to the number you registered with. After landing, many phones are on a new eSIM or have roaming off, so the SMS to your home number never arrives.
steps: Make sure the SIM that owns your registered number can receive texts: turn on roaming for that line, or switch it back on if you disabled it for an eSIM.
On the code screen choose the voice-call option if offered. Alipay can read the code out in an automated call.
Wait 60 seconds before requesting again. Repeated taps can lock requests for a few minutes.
Check your country code is correct on the login screen and that the number has no leading zero.
entries.fallback: If your home number cannot receive texts in China at all, you cannot log in until it can: turn roaming on for that line, or contact Alipay support at +86 571 2688 6000 to change the registered number.

entries.title: Payment failed at the counter
entries.why: Either the shop's amount tripped a limit, your bank declined the charge, or the terminal only reads one payment method. Alipay shows a short reason on the failure screen.
steps: Read the failure line. Issuer declined or Bank declined means your bank: retry once, then call the bank to allow transactions in China.
Limit exceeded means you have hit the unverified allowance. Complete Identity Verification in Me > Settings > Account & Security, then pay again.
If the amount is above 200 RMB, expect a fee line on the confirmation screen before you confirm. Approve it.
If nothing is shown, close and reopen Alipay, then tap Pay/Receive again. Let the cashier scan your code instead of you scanning theirs.
entries.fallback: Pay with cash. Every merchant in China must accept RMB cash by law. Withdraw at a Bank of China ATM with your foreign card.

entries.title: Alipay asks for your passport
entries.why: Chinese rules let you spend a small total without ID. Past that, or for larger single payments, Alipay must verify your passport before it lets the payment through.
steps: Tap Me > Settings > Account & Security > Identity Verification.
Choose passport, photograph the photo page in good light with all four corners visible, then follow the face check.
Wait for the result. It usually completes within the hour; the app allows up to 72 hours.
Retry the payment once the status shows verified.
entries.fallback: If verification is rejected, retake the passport photo without glare and make sure the name you typed matches the passport exactly. If it fails twice, contact Alipay support at +86 571 2688 6000.

entries.title: Use TourCard when your card won't link
entries.why: TourCard is a prepaid wallet inside Alipay issued by a Chinese bank. You top it up from your foreign card, so it works even when direct card linking is refused. It costs more per top-up.
steps: In Alipay, type TourCard in the top search bar and open the mini-program.
Register with your passport when prompted.
Top up from a Visa, Mastercard, JCB or Diners Club card. A service charge is added to each top-up; the exact rate is shown before you confirm.
Pay as usual with Pay/Receive or Scan. TourCard is for paying merchants only, not for sending money to people.
entries.fallback: If TourCard also refuses your card, use cash from a Bank of China ATM, or check whether your home e-wallet is part of the Alipay+ network and can scan Chinese codes directly.

entries.title: How to pay at a shop with Alipay
entries.why: There are two directions: the cashier scans you, or you scan the shop's printed code. Small stalls usually have a printed code; chains and taxis scan you.
steps: To be scanned: open Alipay, tap Pay/Receive at the top, hold the barcode and QR code to the scanner. Enter your 6-digit payment password if asked.
To scan them: tap Scan, point at the shop's printed QR code, type the amount the cashier tells you, confirm.
Check the confirmation screen for the amount and any fee line, then confirm.
Online, choose Alipay at checkout; the site opens the app or shows a QR code for you to scan.
entries.fallback: If the code will not scan, ask the cashier to scan yours instead, or pay cash.

entries.title: Call a DiDi ride from inside Alipay
entries.why: DiDi inside Alipay needs no Chinese phone number and charges your linked card automatically. The WeChat version of DiDi may refuse accounts without a Chinese number.
steps: Open Alipay and type DiDi in the top search bar, or tap the DiDi icon on the home screen.
Allow location, confirm the pickup pin, type the destination in English or Chinese.
Pick a ride type (Express is the cheapest), confirm. The fare is charged to your linked card after the ride.
When the car arrives, match the licence plate with the one shown. The driver may ask for the last 4 digits of your phone number; show them on screen.
entries.fallback: Use the in-app chat; messages are translated automatically. For help, DiDi has 24/7 English support under Account > Help.
